contributions.detail: EMPTY SCHEDULE, not a gap. Form A (p2) carries no ledger ink at all: the filer drew one large S-shaped stroke down the full height of the sheet and wrote 'Didn't Run' across the top rows. Per the addendum that is the filer striking the schedule out - an empty schedule with zero rows, never a row and never a zero-valued transaction. The cover agrees: every one of the twelve cells (four lines x three columns) is a cursive zero glyph, so line 1 is 0 in the THIS and CUMULATIVE columns alike (the two scopes coincide). Zero rows sum to the printed 0.

expenditures.detail: EMPTY SCHEDULE. Form B (p3) is struck out the same way - one large S-stroke down the sheet plus 'Didn't Run' - with no ledger ink. Cover line 3 is a zero glyph in all three columns. Zero rows against a printed 0.

Zero rows emitted on both sides, which matches.

escalation_note: 600 dpi crops of the cover totals block and of Form A's upper band. The cover crop was needed to establish that the twelve marks are cursive ZERO glyphs (which the repo-wide ruling reads as 0) and not dashes (which would stay blank); at 600 dpi they are closed loops with an entry stroke, i.e. zeros. The Form A crop confirmed that the sweeping stroke is a strike-out and that the words read 'Didn't Run'.
